headline: Target holiday comps fall 2.5% as transactions drop 2.9%, but trends improved late; new CEO guides to ~2% sales growth in 2026.
guidance_note: FY26: net sales growth ~2% with small comp increase, GAAP/adj EPS $7.50-8.50, op margin ~20bps above 2025's 4.6% adjusted rate; sales growth expected every quarter.
key_messages: Q4 comps -2.5% (stores -3.9%, digital +1.9%); transactions -2.9% partly offset by +0.4% average ticket.
Management said sales and traffic trends accelerated in the last two months of the quarter and February sales rose.
Gross margin 26.6% vs 26.2% on lower shrink and fulfillment costs, partly offset by markdowns.
FY2025 net sales -1.7% to $104.8B with comps -2.6%; adjusted EPS $7.57 vs $8.86.
Adjusted EPS $2.44 beat ~$2.16 consensus; GAAP EPS $2.30 includes transformation costs.

consumer.big_ticket: Discretionary categories such as apparel and home remained soft through the holiday quarter.

macro_read: Holiday 2025 was weak for Target's discretionary mix, with fewer transactions, but a late-quarter pickup hinted at stabilizing goods demand going into 2026.
